differentiation.support: Provide the student notes open at the series and parallel definitions so learners can follow one path versus branches before deciding which arrangement a house should use.

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to name which scene proved that current is the same on both sides of the bulb before they take the exit ticket.

assessmentPoints: Loop answers in the opening activity
Worksheet answers checked in the closing activity
successCriteria: I can describe a circuit as one unbroken loop of components joined by wires
I can state that the battery pushes charge around the loop, the bulb turns electrical energy into light, and the ammeter measures the flow
objectives.text: Describe a simple circuit as one unbroken loop and state what the battery, bulb and ammeter each do

assessmentPoints: Terminal answers in the second activity
Series-parallel answers in the third activity
successCriteria: I can state that conventional current flows out of the battery's positive terminal, around the loop, and back into the negative terminal
I can explain that in series there is only one path, while in parallel each bulb sits on its own branch
objectives.text: State the direction of conventional current and compare series and parallel circuits

assessmentPoints: Ohm's law answers in the fourth activity
Trap answers in the fifth activity and the closing exit ticket
successCriteria: I can calculate current from V = I R, as 12 divided by 4 is 3 amps for a 12 volt battery across 4 ohms
I can explain that an ammeter reads the same 0.5 amps on both sides of the bulb because current is not used up
objectives.text: Use Ohm's law, V = I R, to calculate current and explain why current is the same everywhere in a series loop

subject: science
title: Electricity: circuits, current and Ohm's law
